title: Fundamental-theorem bound for a Lipschitz curve: ||W(t) - W(s)|| <= ∫_{(-a,a)} ||W'||
statement: Let l be a natural number, W : R -> R^l (R^l = EuclideanSpace R (Fin l)), a a real number and K >= 0, and suppose W is K-Lipschitz on the closed interval [-a, a]. Then for all s, t in [-a, a]: ||W(t) - W(s)|| <= ∫_{(-a,a)} ||deriv W r|| dr. Here deriv is Mathlib's derivative (0 where W is not differentiable), and the integral is the Bochner integral for Lebesgue measure on the open interval (-a, a).
lean_statement: ∀ (ℓ : ℕ) (W : ℝ → Rn ℓ) (a : ℝ) (K : ℝ≥0), LipschitzOnWith K W (Icc (-a) a) → ∀ s ∈ Icc (-a) a, ∀ t ∈ Icc (-a) a, ‖W t - W s‖ ≤ ∫ r in Ioo (-a) a, ‖deriv W r‖
